scenes.tts: Three sensory neuron atlases report eleven, seventeen and eighteen groups. Which count should you trust? Watch the same question change as the evidence changes.
scenes.caption: Three sensory-neuron atlases report eleven, seventeen and eighteen groups. Which count should you trust? Watch the same question change as the evidence changes.
scenes.visual: Hook first. Fill the frame with one schematic dorsal root ganglion containing drifting neuron dots. Three counters, 11, 17 and 18, slide above it and pull against one question mark. Label the whole picture ‘schematic’. Colour map for both chapters: neuron/type blue, RNA profile teal, genetic label gold, physiology green, injury state red, uncertainty grey. Keep dots drifting.
scenes.narration: Three sensory-neuron atlases report eleven, seventeen and eighteen groups. Which count should you trust? Watch the same question change as the evidence changes.

scenes.visual: Transform the three counters into the title ‘From Cluster to Cell Type’. Keep the ganglion and moving dots faintly behind the title; do not cut to an empty card.

scenes.tts: Each dot is one mouse dorsal root ganglion neuron. Its measured RNA becomes a teal barcode. A clustering method groups similar barcodes. Similar barcodes suggest similar molecular programs, but they do not reveal a job by themselves. The result is a map of this sample, not a finished catalogue of nature.
scenes.visual: Zoom into several blue neuron dots. Teal barcode strips grow beside them, then the dots glide into three broad branches of one large schematic tree. A small tag reads ‘this sample’. Branches sway gently while narration continues.
scenes.narration: Each dot is one mouse dorsal root ganglion neuron. Its measured RNA becomes a teal barcode. A clustering method groups similar barcodes. Similar barcodes suggest similar molecular programs, but they do not reveal a job by themselves. The result is a map of this sample, not a finished catalogue of nature.

scenes.tts: Now keep every neuron and every RNA count unchanged. Turn the clustering resolution higher. Will the tree gain neurons, lose neurons, or split existing branches?
scenes.visual: Hold the same tree and dot count. A large resolution dial appears at centre, still untouched. Put the three choices around it as short labels. Dots continue a slow pulse.
scenes.narration: Now keep every neuron and every RNA count unchanged. Turn the clustering resolution higher. Will the tree gain neurons, lose neurons, or split existing branches?

scenes.visual: Keep the question and all three choices visible. The resolution dial glows slowly, but do not reveal the answer.

scenes.tts: It splits branches. No new neuron appeared. That simple dial shows how resolution can change a count. In real atlases, one mouse data set resolved eleven classes, and a larger census resolved seventeen. A cross species integration later reported eighteen dorsal root ganglion subtypes. Those counts also differ in sample and method.
scenes.caption: It splits branches. No new neuron appeared. That simple dial shows how resolution can change a count. In real atlases, one mouse data set resolved eleven classes, and a larger census resolved seventeen. A cross-species integration later reported eighteen dorsal root ganglion subtypes. Those counts also differ in sample and method.
scenes.visual: Turn the dial upward. For the hypothetical, the same three branches divide while a fixed total-dot counter stays constant. Then release that counter and transform it into three separate tags: ‘11: 622 mouse neurons’, ‘17: larger mouse census’ and ‘18: cross-species integration’. Mark all three ‘different data and methods’; do not imply equal samples.
scenes.narration: It splits branches. No new neuron appeared. That simple dial shows how resolution can change a count. In real atlases, one mouse data set resolved eleven classes, and a larger census resolved seventeen. A cross-species integration later reported eighteen dorsal root ganglion subtypes. Those counts also differ in sample and method.

scenes.tts: Resolution is only one control. Whole cells and nuclei capture different RNA, so preparation can hide a branch. A sample can also miss rare cells before clustering even begins. Injury can pull several established types into one red transcriptional state. Neither change is simply extra zoom.
scenes.visual: Add two more large controls beside the resolution dial. A ‘whole cell / nucleus’ filter makes selected teal barcodes fade. Then a red injury magnet pulls dots from several blue branches into one red island while their blue outlines remain visible. Label every grouping ‘schematic’.
scenes.narration: Resolution is only one control. Whole cells and nuclei capture different RNA, so preparation can hide a branch. A sample can also miss rare cells before clustering even begins. Injury can pull several established types into one red transcriptional state. Neither change is simply extra zoom.

scenes.tts: A transcriptomic cluster is therefore a candidate type. It earns a functional type claim when it recurs and an independent measurement anchors it. Its count and boundary still depend on resolution, preparation and state.
scenes.visual: Select one blue branch and enlarge it. Attach two empty sockets labelled ‘recurs’ and ‘independent anchor’. Resolution, preparation and state remain as three moving controls along the bottom.
scenes.narration: A transcriptomic cluster is therefore a candidate type. It earns a functional type claim when it recurs and an independent measurement anchors it. Its count and boundary still depend on resolution, preparation and state.

scenes.tts: Genetic access supplies that test in mice. A marker from the teal RNA profile drives a gold label in the candidate cells. If one marker is too broad, requiring two expression histories narrows the label to their intersection.
scenes.visual: A teal marker badge travels from the selected branch into a gold reporter switch. Several cells turn gold. Then two overlapping marker circles close like an iris, leaving only their overlap gold. Transform the existing branch; do not replace the world.
scenes.narration: Genetic access supplies that test in mice. A marker from the teal RNA profile drives a gold label in the candidate cells. If one marker is too broad, requiring two expression histories narrows the label to their intersection.

scenes.tts: Researchers can follow those labelled endings into skin, then stimulate the skin while imaging the ganglion. In one toolkit, labelled subtypes covered different tested ranges of force and temperature. A distinct ending or response range is independent of the clustering settings. It strengthens the type claim without making every cell identical.
scenes.visual: Extend gold axons from the selected ganglion branch into a large schematic skin cross-section. A probe indents the skin while green calcium glows rise in labelled cell bodies. Show response ranges as broad green bands marked ‘schematic’, never as measured curves. Fill most of the frame.
scenes.narration: Researchers can follow those labelled endings into skin, then stimulate the skin while imaging the ganglion. In one toolkit, labelled subtypes covered different tested ranges of force and temperature. A distinct ending or response range is independent of the clustering settings. It strengthens the type claim without making every cell identical.

scenes.tts: The test still has limits. A driver records marker expression, sometimes during a chosen time window. Calcium signals do not count every spike. The result supports a functional type only within the preparation, stimuli and cells actually tested.
scenes.visual: Add a gold time-window shutter over the reporter, then transform one fast spike train into one slow green calcium glow. Three scope brackets close around the picture: ‘preparation’, ‘stimuli’, ‘sampled cells’. Keep the glow gently decaying.
scenes.narration: The test still has limits. A driver records marker expression, sometimes during a chosen time window. Calcium signals do not count every spike. The result supports a functional type only within the preparation, stimuli and cells actually tested.

scenes.tts: So do not ask which atlas won. Ask what produced each boundary, then ask whether another measurement reaches the same group. That turns a cluster from a pattern into a testable biological claim.
scenes.visual: The 11, 17 and 18 counters shrink into method tags. The selected branch keeps both filled sockets: a recurrence tick and a green physiology anchor. Other branches remain candidates with empty sockets.
scenes.narration: So do not ask which atlas won. Ask what produced each boundary, then ask whether another measurement reaches the same group. That turns a cluster from a pattern into a testable biological claim.

scenes.visual: End card over the carried tree. Large line: ‘A cluster needs an independent anchor before it earns type.’ Keep a slow pulse through the anchored branch.
